# A binary and one command, with nothing installed

`rimsky run --service <name>=<path>` spawns the named binary to serve the run
and reaps it when the command returns. No service installed, no daemon started,
no configuration written by hand, no container runtime.

## The template

```yaml
name: spawned-local-service
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: worker
    executor: devsvc
```

`devsvc` is not configured anywhere. The command line supplies it.

## Run it

```bash
rimsky run template.yml --service devsvc=/path/to/devsvc
```

The command exits 0. Its transcript shows the binary announcing itself, serving
the node, and every node reaching `terminal/success`. The spawned process writes
to the command's own error stream, so its log is in the transcript.

A consumer project ships a binary and a one-line wrapper instead of an
installer.

## The binding is what supplies the service

```bash
rimsky run template.yml
```

Without the flag the run does not happen at all: the command exits non-zero at
template registration with a validation failure. Nothing pre-existing on the
machine was serving the node.

## Gone when the run returns

When the command returns, the process that served the run is gone, no process
anywhere is running the bound binary, and no rimsky process from the command is
left behind.

A second invocation of the same command is served by a different process, which
is likewise gone when it returns.

Nothing accumulates on the developer's machine between runs: no daemon to stop,
no state to clean up.
